title: Dolores Huerta, farmworker organizer, dies at 96
caption: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the farmworkers' union that became the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez in 1962, died Oct. 28 at her home in Bakersfield, California, at 96; her family said the cause was cancer. Shown in tribute: the 1960s Delano grape strike picket line she marched on. She coined the rallying cry "Sí se puede" and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.

stories.name: Labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
facts: Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 96, at her home in Bakersfield, California, surrounded by family; a family spokesperson said the cause was cancer.
In 1962 she and Cesar Chavez founded the National Farm Workers Association, which became the United Farm Workers; she served as its vice president until 1999.

She joined Filipino grape pickers on the picket line in the five-year Delano grape strike and led national grape and lettuce boycotts in the early 1970s, which helped win California's 1975 law recognizing farmworkers' right to bargain collectively.
She coined the rallying cry 'Sí se puede'. President Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.

artwork.alt: Graphic poster illustration of a 1960s farmworkers' picket line on a California vineyard road at sunset. A young Dolores Huerta, with long dark hair and a red top, leads the line with one arm raised in front of a huge setting sun, followed by six farmworkers in work clothes and caps. Vine rows run to the horizon, grape clusters frame the corners, and long shadows stretch toward the viewer. A historical tribute marking her death at 96.
